harnessProvenance.change: The first 14 successful rows use the original harness. Its pitch-bounded pass-target validator rejected legal out-of-play physical targets in subsequent matches. The resumed version uses the existing finite physicalPointSchema and validates/skips saved results. Simulation, measurements, thresholds and outcome definitions are unchanged; each saved result retains its actual harness hash.

definitions.depth: Target >0.5m beyond actual legal release snapshot line, with defender/ball/halfway rule. Contact beyond release line is separate from a completed pass received earlier. Also report contact beyond the second-last defender at resolution, excluding ball from that latter line.
definitions.fallbacks: Count passes whose matching release snapshot was unavailable; preceding 0.025s frame used. Tolerance0.5m, no estimate relabelled exact.
definitions.carry: One continuous wide carry/possession episode starting with active physical carry intention and nearest eligible opponent within8m, initially no more than1m behind. Intent refreshes do not create a new episode. End on deliberate pass/cross/shot, opponent/teammate acquisition, departure/stoppage, or loose ball without ownership for1.5s. Passing marker requires >1m goalward lead and >1m actor movement with actual control; later loss remains possible. This is not a provider-defined successful-dribble statistic.
definitions.replay: Thirty complete state/tick/official identity equalities against the original observed cohort. Replays add no independent fixtures or new validation sample.
definitions.completions: Raw replay summaries retain the physical diagnostic outcome. Final comparison completion requires actual contact and resolution, a distinct intended receiver and a receiver other than the passer, exactly as playerMatchStats.ts. A passer collecting his own delivery is a self-recovery, not a completed pass; targeted self-recoveries are included in failed pass totals and reported separately. All thirty complete official completion counts reconcile.
